title: Drop the beacon probe (probe console, left)

text: First item on today's plan: drop beacon probe K-1 and log its signal.
Einstein's field equation. Matter tells spacetime how to curve; curved spacetime tells matter how to move.
Someone has worked it out underneath: at ten horizon radii our clocks run at 0.949 of the relay's. Every hour here is about an hour and three minutes out there.
The archive holds the expedition's training simulations. Same equations as outside the window, slowed down so you can take them apart.
The probe console is the one on the left, by the window. Walk up to it and use it.
Back already, Doctor? You were talking in your sleep last night. Something about falling. I did not log it.
Cold coffee. Six hours old by my watch.
Six hours and twenty minutes by the relay's. Hovering this close to Erebus, every clock aboard runs about five percent slow.
The black disk is Erebus's shadow. It is about two and a half times wider than the horizon itself.
